title: Gen IV/V Add Item
doc_note: Device steps for round-2 candidate (host-verified, NOT device-verified): 1. Open a Diamond/Pearl/Platinum or HeartGold/SoulSilver save, then a Black/White or Black 2/White 2 save. 2. Bag → pick a pocket with free space → Add Item → choose a stackable item (e.g. Potion). 3. Expect: the item appears in the pocket with quantity 1 *before* any quantity prompt; A on that row edits the quantity, B leaves it at 1. 4. Repeat with a unique item (a Key Item): it is added with quantity 1 and offers no quantity editor. 5. Review Pending Changes lists the addition; Discard removes it; the source save is unchanged. title: Shiny vs non-shiny stat rerolls
doc_note: Device steps for round-2 candidate (host-verified, NOT device-verified): 1. Gen I/II: edit a non-shiny Pokémon, press **Y** several times: DVs change immediately, no confirm, the Pokémon stays non-shiny. Repeat on a shiny one: it stays shiny (Gen II), and Gen II gender and the Unown letter follow the DVs. 2. Gen III–V: same on a non-shiny and a shiny Pokémon: IVs change immediately; shininess, gender, nature and (Gen III) Unown letter are preserved. 3. Discard; the source save is unchanged. What to expect, and why (Lane R, `docs/REROLL_MECHANICS.md`): in Gen I/II a shiny and a non-shiny can never have the same DVs, because shininess is the DV pattern itself (Defense, Speed, Special DV 10; Attack DV 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14 or 15). In Gen III–V shininess comes from the PID and IDs, not the IVs, so a shiny and a non-shiny *can* have identical IVs/EVs; that is correct, not a bug. Host check: CG06 (enforced) and Lane R `tests/test_reroll_mechanics_gen15.cpp` (100 rerolls per case in every generation; lane push `951a8993`, not yet on #307).

title: Origin & Legality wording
doc_note: Round 3 device steps (host-verified, NOT device-verified): **Device steps** 1. Use one save per generation, Gen I to V. Open a Pokémon, then Actions. 2. The row is labelled **Origin & Legality**. The modal heading and the right-hand provenance pane use the same words. 3. None of "Encounter legality", "Legality & Provenance" or "Deep encounter legality" appears anywhere. **Host evidence** - CG03 `origin-legality-heading` (enforced) requires the exact heading in all five generations and bans the three old strings in UI sources. - The hardware gate pins CG03 for the round-1 accepted items. **Known gap (Part 9, report 1):** Gen V Actions has **no** Origin & Legality row, while Gen IV does (`Gen4SharedPokemonSurface.inc:954`). On a Black/White save, expect the heading only where a provenance pane exists. Report the missing row as part of S03/S's Gen V parity, not as an E03 regression.

title: Rerolls keep the requested Shiny / Gender
doc_note: Round 3 device steps (host-verified, NOT device-verified): **Device steps** 1. Gen I/II: edit a non-shiny Pokémon and press **Y** several times. - The DVs change at once, with no confirm, and the Pokémon stays non-shiny. - On a shiny one, it stays shiny (Gen II). - In Gen II, gender and the Unown letter follow the DVs. 2. Gen III–V: do the same on a non-shiny and a shiny Pokémon. - The IVs change at once. - Shininess, gender, nature and (Gen III) the Unown letter are kept. 3. Discard. The source save is unchanged. **Host evidence** - CG06 `reroll-without-confirmation` (enforced). - `tests/test_reroll_mechanics_gen15.cpp` (lane R, now in `host-test`): 100+ rerolls per shiny and non-shiny case in every generation. - `tests/test_gen12_dv_reroll.cpp` and `tests/test_shared_stat_reroll.cpp` (in `host-test`). - Acceptance-matrix `reroll` cells: PASS in all 20 versions. In Gen I/II a shiny and a non-shiny can never share DVs, because shininess *is* the DV pattern. In Gen III–V shininess comes from the PID and IDs, so identical IVs are correct (`docs/REROLL_MECHANICS.md`).

title: Party / summary-panel taps
doc_note: Round 3 device steps (host-verified, NOT device-verified): **Device steps** 1. In a Gen III, IV and V save, open Boxes and tap the selected Pokémon's summary panel. Then open Party and tap a Pokémon. 2. Each opens that game's own Actions sheet, with no "Make Shiny" row and no flash of a generic View. 3. In a Gen I/II save, do the same. The generation's own sheet/View opens. **Host evidence** - `tests/test_party_summary_tap_routing.cpp` (in `host-test`) walks the Gen III/IV and Gen V routing rules over every hit id the box panel publishes. It also reads the shipped call sites: summary id 2000 and the party taps reach the native Actions path before any generic fallthrough. - CG11 (enforced): no generic action sheet or details modal opens in a Gen I–V session. **Not covered on host:** Gen I/II taps have no routing test of their own; CG11 is their only host guard.

title: The exported edited save loads in an emulator
doc_note: Round 3 device steps (host-verified, NOT device-verified): **Device steps** 1. Take the export from S04 (Black/White) and one export each from Gen I–IV. 2. Load each in the emulator as a **separate** save. Never overwrite the original. 3. The edits are present and the game reports no corrupted save. 4. Load the original save. It is unchanged. **Host evidence, all 20 games** (acceptance matrix, `make -f Makefile.host qa-matrix`, GCC + clang, plain + ASan/UBSan): - The `export` cell publishes into a new directory: - `original_backup.*` equals the source; - `edited.*` **strictly reparses** as the exact game with the edit; - only whitelisted record/block/checksum bytes differ; - a second export gets a new directory. - Round 3 adds `exportCorruptionProbe`. A copy of `edited.*` with one checksummed byte changed must **stop** reparsing as the edited save. That proves the reparse checks the checksum an emulator checks, on the exact bytes written. The runner fails unless all 20 versions record `export.checksum=detects-corruption` (see [GEN1_5_MATRIX.md](../qa/GEN1_5_MATRIX.md), "Round 3"). - The `immutability` cell: source bytes, size and nanosecond mtime are unchanged after discovery, linking, every edit and the export, in all 20 games. - Export contracts C1–C5 (`tests/test_qa_export_contracts.cpp`). This is evidence that the file is internally consistent. It is **not** evidence that an emulator accepts it.

title: Gen V Create/Edit/Clone/Move/Release parity
doc_note: Verdict: **REPRODUCES (partial)**; owning lane: S. 1. **Gen V parity.** Clone, Move and Release are offered only when `workspace.originalOccupied(slot)` is true (`include/Integration/Gen5/Gen5SharedEditorBridge.h:59-68`). That check is false for a slot with a pending change (`Gen5StagedPokemonWorkspace.h:226-231`). A host probe showed: - an original slot gets `[View] [Edit] [Clone] [Move Pokemon] [Remove] [Cancel]`; - a cloned or created slot gets only `[View] [Edit] [Review Pending Changes] [Cancel]`. Gen IV works from the reparsed staged buffer (`Gen4StagedPokemonEditor.cpp:421-438, 551-560`). Gen V Move also uses Box/Slot number prompts (`Gen5SharedReadOnlySurface.inc:1216-1238`), where Gen IV uses the shared ClassicPackedMove carry. Gen V has no Origin & Legality row (Gen IV: `Gen4SharedPokemonSurface.inc:954`). **Fix:** base eligibility on the staged view, and route Move through ClassicPackedMove.
later_refs: Lane S 06a7dce: fixed on lane branch (not yet on #307)

title: Gen V species picker sprites, shiny preview, restrictions
doc_note: Verdict: Does not reproduce in source; sprites for 494-649 need a device check; owning lane: —. 2. **Species picker.** It is the shared picker, species 1-649, with a Y toggle for Normal/Shiny (`SharedSpeciesPicker.h:389-430`). Ineligible picks are refused after the choice (`Gen5SharedScreenState.h:399-419`), the same as Gen III/IV. `tools/check_device_assets.py` checks shiny sprites only for Gen I (lines 178-179), so the Gen V shiny art is unchecked.

title: Generic emulator labels
doc_note: Verdict: **REPRODUCES on the Trainer / Game Browser** (corrected); owning lane: 2R. 3. **Emulator labels.** Home cards show the provider name: DraStic, melonDS, RetroArch, or "RetroArch (DeSmuME)" (`SaveProviderIdentity.h:66-142`). `test_home_card_providers` passes. The Trainer / Game Browser header does **not** (see Corrections).

title: RetroArch/DraStic launch and exit
doc_note: Verdict: **REPRODUCES**: the return-to-app opt-in is by design, but there is also a source defect in core choice (corrected); owning lane: 2R / L. 4. **Launch/exit.** The return host runs only when `<configRoot>/experimental_return_host.enable` exists (`GameLauncher.cpp:38-41, 1258-1268`). By default the Home confirm says that quitting the emulator returns to the Homebrew Menu, or to DraStic's own launcher. With the marker present, the plan returns to PokeBank NX. This is intended until the return host is validated on device.

title: Touch Quick View drag / modal isolation
doc_note: Verdict: Does not reproduce on host; drag feel needs a device; owning lane: P (test gap). 5. **Touch.** No "Quick View" surface exists. View/Edit drag, panel swipe and modal layering are wired (`SharedPokemonEditorSurface.inc:533-617`; `ScreenChrome.h:306, 408-418`). Gen V Review draws without `beginModal` (`Gen5SharedReadOnlySurface.inc:1673-1676`), but it only accepts keys. **Gap:** `tests/test_touch_scroll_state.cpp` is in no `Makefile.host*`. It passes when built by hand.

title: TM/HM/Mail/Ball/item sprites
doc_note: Verdict: **REPRODUCES (Gen V only)**; owning lane: I. 6. **Item sprites.** `test_item_sprite_coverage.py` passes for Gen I-IV: 124/221/307/514 eligible, 0 missing. Gen V is not covered by that test. Findings for Gen V: - 7 feathers have no icon (ids 565-571). The pinned art exists as `*-wing`, so only the aliases are missing. - All 101 TMs/HMs have no icon. `MachineDisplay.cpp:32-112` has no BW/B2W2 case, and `ClassicMachineArtwork.h:109` returns type 0. - HM01-06 (ids 420-425) are labelled "TM93".."TM98", the BDSP names, so they read as duplicate TM93-98 (`ItemNames.cpp:429-434`). A host probe printed `game=BW id=420 label='TM93'`. **Fix:** add BW/B2W2 machine mapping (TM01-92 = 328-419, HM01-06 = 420-425, TM93-95 = 618-620) and the feather to wing aliases, and extend coverage to Gen V. Citation to verify against the pinned PKHeX item tables before landing.

title: Gen V save-instance profile assignment

title: Gen IV multi-select Move / Y
doc_note: Verdict: **REPRODUCES in the Storage view**; owning lane: S. 8. **Gen IV Storage view.** In the save pane: - Y is stripped as read-only (`TrainerViewScreenBase.inc:2369-2372`). - Actions → Move picks up from `stSaveBox/stSaveSlot` (`Gen4SharedPokemonSurface.inc:276`), but `placeGen4` drops at the Boxes-tab cursor (`ClassicPackedMoveOverlay.inc:604-605`). - No carry is drawn there (`:982`; `StoragePanel.cpp` never calls `hidesGen4CarriedSource`). The Boxes view works and is covered by `test_gen4_hardware_surface_contract`. **Fix:** use the Storage cursor for pickup, drop and the drawn carry, or send Move to Boxes, and keep Y when a staged Gen IV editor exists.

title: S06 deferral is not write permission
doc_note: The owner deferred S06 on purpose. It is not permission for direct writing or injection.

title: Origin & Legality wording
doc_note: Steps: In one save per generation (I–V), open a Pokémon → Actions → Origin & Legality. Expected: The row and panel say "Origin & Legality". The state is honest (never "Legality OK" for an unchecked record).

title: Backup deletion is protected
doc_note: Steps: Open Backups. Try to delete a backup, then the original save entry. Expected: Deleting a backup asks first (Y confirms, B cancels). The original save cannot be deleted.

title: Gen IV move Category spacing
doc_note: Steps: Gen IV save → Pokémon → Moves. Expected: The Category element does not crowd the type badge or the Power / Accuracy section.

title: Pokémon Actions order
doc_note: Steps: Open Actions from Boxes and from Party in each generation. Expected: The same order everywhere; Party shows View / Edit / Origin & Legality / Cancel.

title: Gen III/IV Trainer Name and Money reach Review
doc_note: Steps: Gen III and Gen IV save → Trainer → change Name and Money → open Review → leave. Expected: Both changes are listed by name; leaving offers the four staged-exit actions.

title: No "Touch: Back" footer
doc_note: Steps: Open View / Overview and a few windows. Expected: No "Touch: Back" text; tapping Back still works.

title: Bag Remove and Key Item warning buttons
doc_note: Steps: Bag → select an item → Remove; also a Key Item. Expected: Coloured A / B glyph buttons inside the dialog; A removes, B cancels; no repeat in the footer.

title: Gen II PC Move
doc_note: Steps: Gold / Silver / Crystal → Boxes → move a Pokémon between slots and between boxes. Expected: Pick up, drop and cancel all complete; Review lists the move.

title: Species keyboard beside the list
doc_note: Steps: Create or Edit → Species → open the search keyboard. Expected: The keyboard sits under the species art; the whole list stays visible.

title: Held Item search and Sort
doc_note: Steps: Held Item picker → − (Search) → type POKE, then clear; X to sort. Expected: Docked keyboard beside the results; live filtering; Sort works; B closes the keys.

title: Crystal OT Gender inline
doc_note: Steps: Crystal → Edit a Pokémon → OT Gender → press A. Expected: It cycles inline; no three-option popup.

title: Ball picker scrollbar gutter
doc_note: Steps: Edit → Ball. Expected: Rows stop before the scrollbar; the bar has its own space.

title: Nature stat colours
doc_note: Steps: Gen III–V → a Pokémon with a non-neutral Nature → Stats; then open the Nature picker. Expected: The raised stat is green and the lowered stat red, in the stats and the picker's +10% / −10% line.

title: Selected species name first
doc_note: Steps: Select a species. Expected: The left panel reads "Pikachu" or "Pikachu #25", never "25 Pikachu"; lists keep their numbers.

title: Gen IV/V location choices
doc_note: Steps: Gen IV / V → Met Location for a wild-catchable species (e.g. Walrein). Expected: Wild data for the species and its ancestry first; other native histories marked unverified; nothing legitimate refused.

title: Ability names and effects
doc_note: Steps: Gen III–V → Ability picker. Expected: Ability names with full effects, never "Slot 1/2"; slot restrictions respected.

title: Create defaults
doc_note: Steps: Create a Pokémon in Gen I/II and in Gen III–V. Expected: DVs 0 (Gen I/II) and IVs 0 (Gen III–V); existing Pokémon unchanged.

title: Gen V Home A opens the assigned save
doc_note: Steps: HOME → Gen V card → A. Expected: The assigned save opens directly, with no second save chooser.

title: Gen V Key Items and TMs editable
doc_note: Steps: Gen V → Bag → Key Items and TMs & HMs → Add / Remove. Expected: Staged Add / Remove works, with the Key Item warning; no blanket view-only footer.

title: Gen I–IV staged exit menu
doc_note: Steps: Stage any change → leave with B. Expected: A Review, B Continue, Y Discard & Exit, X Export Copy.

title: Gen I–III Party Actions popup
doc_note: Steps: Party → A or tap a Pokémon. Expected: View / Edit / Origin & Legality / Cancel, not straight to View.

title: Gen II Special *(restyled in round 6: 7A)*
doc_note: Steps: Gen II → Edit → Stats → change the Special DV and the Special Stat Exp. Expected: One Special DV and one Stat Exp; calculated SpA and SpD both update and differ where the bases differ.

title: Gen III Create with Safari Ball
doc_note: Steps: Gen III (FRLG and one RSE) → Create Pikachu → Ball: Safari → Keep → Review → Export → reopen the export. Expected: Safari is accepted as the caught Ball; Review names the values; the export reopens with them.

title: Gen V move pools *(restyled in round 6: 7B)*
doc_note: Steps: Gen V → Pikachu → Moves; also Wormadam, Rotom, B2W2 Kyurem. Expected: Species / form pools only (not 559 moves); Learnable / Transfer / Prior form / Preserved meanings intact.

title: Original saves never change
doc_note: Steps: Open a save, edit, export, discard; reopen the original. Expected: The original is unchanged; the edit exists only in the export.

title: Met Location rows fit
doc_note: Steps: Gen III–V → Met Location; scroll the whole list. Expected: Every row shows in full, with no "…"; row 1 is the stored location.

title: Gen V Language inline *(restyled in round 6: 7C)*
doc_note: Steps: Gen V → Edit → Language → A, and a completed tap. Expected: It cycles inline through supported languages, stays staged and appears by name in Review.

title: Backups list and open
doc_note: Steps: Open Backups (emulator and Switch). Open an older copy, edit Money, export, discard, reopen the copy. Expected: Full-screen list, newest first; A opens that exact copy as a staged session; the copy keeps its Money.

title: A selects and advances
doc_note: Steps: Use A across HOME, Game Browser and editors. Expected: A selects and advances normally; the assigned Gen V save opens directly.

title: Trainer Play Time and Gender *(restyled in round 6: P2)*
doc_note: Steps: Gen II–IV → Trainer → edit Play Time; Crystal / Gen III / Gen IV → Gender → Review → Export → reopen. Expected: Changes are staged, named in Review, and present only in the export; no Gender in Gen I or Gold / Silver.

title: Help names real controls *(restyled in round 6: P4)*
doc_note: Steps: Open Help on the Pokémon, Items and Trainer pages in each generation. Expected: Every control named does that action there; no "+ Review" where + does something else.

title: Pokérus and Held Item selection
doc_note: Steps: 1. Gen III and Gen V: Edit → Pokérus; tap its row (also after scrolling) and press A. 2. Gen III: Held Item picker → choose an item with A, then with a tap, at the top, middle and bottom of the list. Expected: Pokérus can be changed in Gen III and V as in Gen II / IV; a tap does what A does and a swipe only scrolls. Every Held Item choice is applied with A and with a tap, at any list position.

title: Gold / Silver Trainer layout
doc_note: Steps: Gold and Silver → Trainer; also Crystal. Expected: No overlapping rows; no "Male" label under another row; no Gender row in Gold / Silver.

title: Bag Review is discoverable
doc_note: Steps: Bag in each generation → find Review without using + or the exit menu. Expected: A visible, labelled Review control in the Bag that opens Review and returns to the Bag.

title: Controller glyphs and footers
doc_note: Steps: Look at the footers and Help in HOME, Game Browser (Controls), Party, Boxes, Trainer, Bag, Create, Edit, Review and Backups. Expected: Every action shows a coloured glyph; every glyph shown does something there; Game Browser Help has no stale Review lines.

title: Gen V event and location rows distinguishable
doc_note: Steps: Black 2 / White 2 → Met Location → scroll to the POKÉPARK and Festa rows. Expected: No two rows read the same; repeated names carry what tells them apart (year, location id or source); unknown provenance says so.

title: Older Trainer cards match Gen V
doc_note: Steps: Trainer in Gen I, II, III and IV, next to Gen V. Expected: The same card design and read-only styling; no Gen II Gender overlap; nothing invented for Gen I or Gold / Silver.

title: Gen II Unown letter, shiny and DVs agree
doc_note: Steps: Gen II → an Unown (try A) → toggle Shiny on and off; press Y to reroll a few times. Expected: The letter shown, the sprite and the DVs always agree. If making it shiny must change the letter, the screen says so (letter comes from the DVs).

title: Review is easy to find and returns where it came from
doc_note: Steps: Open Review from Trainer, Create, Edit, Bag, Party and Boxes, in each generation; leave it with B. Expected: A visible Review prompt on each screen; B returns to the screen it was opened from.

title: Gen II Special SpA / SpD placement
doc_note: Steps: Gen II → Edit → Stats. Expected: SpA and SpD are placed clearly; the values match A22.

title: Gen V "Learnable" label
doc_note: Steps: Gen V → Moves → move chooser. Expected: "Learnable" uses the same OK treatment as Gen I–IV.

title: No Gen V Language toast
doc_note: Steps: Gen V → Edit → Language → A. Expected: The value changes inline with no extra toast.

title: Tap outside closes non-destructive popups
doc_note: Steps: Open a picker, Help, or a details popup; tap outside it. Then open a Discard / Delete / Remove confirmation and tap outside. Expected: Non-destructive popups close, and the tap does not also press what was underneath. Destructive confirmations stay open.

title: Save safety and backups
doc_note: Steps: Review the Backups screens and the export flow against PKSE habits. Expected: Nothing overwrites a source save; backups are app-owned, dated and protected.

title: Gen V Trainer visual standard
doc_note: Steps: Compare all Trainer screens (same work as B06). Expected: One visual standard across generations.

title: Bag Review discoverability
doc_note: Steps: Same as B03. Expected: Review is reachable from the Bag without hunting.

title: Gen III held-item policy (Safari Ball / Berry Juice)
doc_note: Steps: 1. Gen III → Create or Edit → Held Item → look for Safari Ball and Berry Juice. 2. Ball → Safari. 3. If you have a save whose Pokémon already holds one, open it. Expected: Safari Ball and Berry Juice cannot be chosen as held items; Safari is still a valid caught Ball; an existing record holding one is kept and labelled honestly; the Bag is unaffected.

title: Gen II Unown letter selector (optional request)
doc_note: Steps: Gen II → Unown → choose a letter. Expected: Choosing a letter picks a valid DV combination for it, keeping the shiny state you asked for where possible, and says when it cannot.

title: Tap-outside: no tap-through
doc_note: Steps: Over the Boxes grid, open a popup and tap outside it on a Pokémon slot. Expected: The popup closes and the slot underneath is not opened or moved.

title: View mode explains instead of doing nothing (L06 follow-up)
doc_note: Steps: Gen III, IV and V → open a Pokémon in **View** (not Edit) → press A on Pokérus, then tap Held Item. Also press A on Origin or PID. Expected: Pokérus / Held Item say "View only: choose Edit to change …". Origin / PID say "… is read-only for this Pokémon". Nothing is staged. (Gen I/II use different screens and are not covered.)

title: Gen V Pokérus on a Pokémon that already has it (L06)
doc_note: Steps: Gen V → Edit a Pokémon that already has Pokérus (infected or cured) → change Pokérus, cycle it back and forth → Keep → Review. Expected: Keep is accepted, Review names the Pokérus state in words, not raw numbers like "2 -> 1".

title: Create Review shows the new Pokémon's details (P3)
doc_note: Steps: In each generation, Create a Pokémon → Keep → open Review. Expected: A header "Add Pokémon: Empty → <Species> Lv n" followed by named rows: Moves, OT / ID, and where the game stores them Held Item, Ball, Nature, Gender, Ability, Language, Met. Only changed IVs/EVs/DVs, Shiny, Pokérus, Friendship appear. Gen I/II never show Nature, Ability or Ball.

title: Gen II Create starts with level-up moves
doc_note: Steps: Gold, Silver or Crystal → Create → Pikachu Lv 5. Expected: Moves start as Thunder Shock and Growl (with PP), as in Gen I and III–V, and Review lists them.

title: Stored unreleased held item is labelled, not deleted
doc_note: Steps: Gen III → open a Pokémon that already holds Safari Ball or Berry Juice (if you have one). Expected: The item shows with "(unreleased)" and is kept; it is not offered as a new choice for other Pokémon.

title: Switching saves never carries a draft over
doc_note: Steps: Open save A → start editing a Pokémon (do not Keep) → leave the save with Discard & Exit → open save B → open its Boxes. Expected: Save B shows no editor, picker or draft from save A; Review of B lists only B's own changes.

title: Gen I–III export refuses a changed original
doc_note: Steps: Open a Gen I–III emulator save in PokeBank → make an edit → (optional, advanced) change the original save file outside the app → Export Copy. Expected: If the original changed since it was opened, the export is refused with a message; otherwise it exports normally. The original is never modified.

title: Gen I–V Review consistency
doc_note: Steps: Stage a named move or item and a Money change in each generation; open Review. Expected: The same pages, names and before / after values in every generation; X Export Copy, Y Discard All, B Back.

title: Gen I Review presentation
doc_note: Steps: Gen I → stage changes → Review; then Y Discard All, and B. Expected: Only the shared Review panel and its confirmation; no old panel or footer on top; a swipe turns one page.

title: Export loads in an emulator (optional)
doc_note: Steps: Load an exported copy in an emulator as a **separate** save. Expected: The edits are present and no corruption is reported; the original is unchanged.

title: Install · Install, open and HOME card
doc_note: Steps: Copy this NRO to the SD card (back up first). Check its SHA-256. Open it from the Homebrew Menu. On Product Home, move the focus onto the selected game card and off it again, in handheld and docked mode, and with two different themes if you like. Expected: The app opens to Product Home. The region picture at the top of the game card follows the card's **rounded top corners**: no square picture corner sticks out past the card's corner or the blue focus ring, focused or not, in handheld and docked. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Quit · Leave and Launch questions
doc_note: Steps: On Product Home press the button that asks to quit (and, if you use it, the Launch game question). Then open a save, stage an edit and back out to the save's exit question. Expected: The quit / launch question has two plain buttons: **B Cancel** on the left (nothing happens) and **Y Quit** (or **Y Launch**). There is no A Stay button. The save exit question labels B as **Cancel**; Save & Exit / Discard / Cancel still work as before. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Move · Move: Y picks up, A places, B cancels (every generation)
doc_note: Steps: In one save per generation you have (I–V), on the Boxes grid pick a Pokémon up (Gen I–IV: Y; Gen V: A → Move), move to an empty slot and press **A**. Repeat once and press **B** instead. Try A on an occupied slot. Expected: A places it; B cancels with nothing changed; A on an occupied slot is refused with a message and nothing is overwritten. Y or X while carrying only shows the hint "A places it here, B cancels". The footer reads A Place / L/R Box / B Cancel. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Clone · Clone is a visual carry (every generation)
doc_note: Steps: Box Pokémon → A → Clone, in each generation you have. Gen V: also clone a Party Pokémon. Expected: The menu closes and you are back on the box carrying a faded "Copy". No number keypad and no menu opens. **Gen III–V:** A on any empty slot places the copy there. **Gen I/II:** boxes have no gaps, so the copy always goes **after the last Pokémon of the box you choose** (the faded copy shows exactly where), and the messages never say you can pick any empty slot. A on an occupied slot is refused; B cancels with nothing staged. The original stays where it was. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Actions · Actions order, Move row and X Export / Import
doc_note: Steps: A on an occupied box slot, in each generation. Then press X on an occupied slot, and X on an empty slot. A on an empty slot. Expected: Every Actions list reads View, Edit, Clone, Move, Release, Origin & Legality, Export to file, (Review), Cancel. Gen II and III now have Move on Boxes. X on an occupied slot exports it to a file; X on an empty slot imports from a file; X never opens Create. A on an empty slot still offers Add Pokémon. Gen I–III Party Actions list Review Pending Changes while changes are staged. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: File browser · "-" cancels Import from file
doc_note: Steps: X on an empty slot (Import from file). Go into a folder, press B, then press **-**. Also open Link Game File on Product Home and press -. Expected: B goes up one folder. **-** closes the browser from anywhere (any folder, Favourites) with nothing imported or linked. The footer shows both. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Create · Create needs a Met Location choice and a move (Gen III–V)
doc_note: Steps: Gen III (FireRed or LeafGreen if you have one), Gen IV and Gen V: Add Pokémon on an empty slot. Pick a species that is not a wild catch in that game (FR/LG: Rayquaza or Charizard). Try Keep without choosing anything. Then open Met Location. Expected: Keep is refused with one message naming what is missing (Met Location and/or at least one move). The new draft starts with **no moves**. The Met Location list is never empty: listed catches come first (with their levels); every other location of that exact game follows, marked **"Not a listed catch; unverified"** (Trade / Egg / Event marked separately). After you choose a location and a move, Keep works. The "one move" rule is a PokeBank requirement, not a legality claim. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Crystal · Crystal Met Location list
doc_note: Steps: Crystal only: edit or create a Pokémon and open its Met Location / caught data. Expected: The list is never empty: catch rows first, then every Johto/Kanto landmark marked unverified. Caught data stays optional (no caught data is a normal traded Pokémon). [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: History · Species change keeps an existing Pokémon's history (H25)
doc_note: Steps: Edit an **existing** Pokémon (Gen III, IV, V or Crystal) that has Pokérus or a known Met Location. Change its species to something unrelated. Look at Origin & Legality, then Keep and open Review. Expected: Pokérus, origin game, Met Location and Met Level are **kept exactly**. If the combination now looks unusual, a **Caution** line says so (for example "Met Location is not a listed catch for <species> (history kept)") in the editor and on its Review entry. Nothing is deleted and Keep is not blocked. For a **new** (Create) draft, a species change shows a status naming what was reset (e.g. "Species changed: Pokérus cleared and Met Location needs a new choice"). [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Top Up · Scope is easy to find; Gen I says its Bag is shared
doc_note: Steps: Bag → ZR (Top Up / Add Missing). Look at the Scope row and change it with Left/Right. Gen I–III: also try PC Items and Bag + PC Items. Gen I: Add Missing on the whole Bag when it is nearly full. Expected: SETUP opens on Scope (`< All Bag pockets >`, or in Gen I `< Whole Bag (20 slots shared) >`). Preview says how many slots were free and how many items did not fit. After A, a partial result says **"Partly staged: … N did not fit because the Bag is full (20 slots shared by every category). Nothing overflowed"**. The Bag never holds more than the game allows. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Recovery files · Selection is visible; nothing starts selected
doc_note: Steps: Open Recovery files from a game. Move the focus, select one removable copy, select another, deselect one. Try A on a protected copy and on a heading. Press - for Help. Expected: Focus starts on the opening game's copies. **Nothing starts selected.** A selected copy is clearly marked (coloured bar and badge), different from the focus outline. Protected copies explain why they are kept and cannot be selected; headings do nothing. The footer shows A Select / Deselect, Y Remove selected (n) only when something is selected, and B Back. Removing still asks both confirmations. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Gen II stats · Special shows Sp. Atk and Sp. Def
doc_note: Steps: Gen II: open a Pokémon's stats. Expected: The Special row's Calculated cell shows two numbers: Sp. Atk then Sp. Def. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Quiet edits · No toast after routine edits; Gen V Shiny inline
doc_note: Steps: In any generation: change the Unown letter, reroll DVs/IVs with Y, toggle Shiny. Gen V: Shiny on the PID panel. Expected: These succeed without a pop-up message (refusals and warnings still show). Gen V Shiny toggles inline like Gender, with no "Change PID?" dialog; gender, nature and ability stay the same. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Gen V names · Localized names and Korean text
doc_note: Steps: Gen V: open a Pokémon from a non-English game or with a non-English language (if you have one). Cycle its Language in the editor without a nickname. Any Korean Gen IV/V Pokémon: look at its name. Expected: The header shows the stored name in its own script (Japanese, Korean, accented French …), and an un-nicknamed name follows the Language. Korean text draws as Hangul, not boxes. Changing Language never changes a nickname or the OT. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Gen V quick view · Radar matches the editor
doc_note: Steps: Gen V Boxes: move the cursor across several Pokémon and watch the quick-view stat radar; then open one in View. Expected: The quick view uses the same radar, scale and values as the editor / View and updates as the cursor moves. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Species picker · One picture, Normal / Shiny
doc_note: Steps: Open the species picker in Create. Press Y (or tap the picture) to switch Normal / Shiny. Gen II: try Unown. Expected: One picture, centred, captioned NORMAL or SHINY. If shiny art is missing it says "No shiny sprite" instead of showing the normal art. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Safety · Review, Keep, Discard and Export Copy
doc_note: Steps: In one save, stage several of the changes above. Open Review, Discard once (answer B, then Y), stage again, then Export Copy. Expected: Review lists every staged change (including any Caution notes). Discard asks first and restores the original. Export Copy writes a separate verified file; the original save is unchanged. A Japanese Gen I/II save (if you have one) stays read-only. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Earlier rounds · Smoke check of Round 11 PASS items
doc_note: Steps: Briefly repeat a few things that passed in Round 11 (open each generation, edit and Keep a Pokémon, Bag Help, Gen IV Bag Remove/Add, search with L/R). Expected: They still behave as they did in Round 11. [Round 12 checklist, NOT DEVICE TESTED]

title: Decision: H25 Edit vs Create
doc_note: Engineering decision applied in the Round 11 campaign ('owner may override'); overridden by the Oct 31 owner safety clarifications where they differ. Text: A new Pokémon draft starts clean, and a species change in Create resets Pokérus and any Met Location that is not valid for the new species. On an **existing** Pokémon, its own history (Met Location, Pokérus) is legitimate and is **kept**; nothing is silently cleared.

title: Decision: Moves
doc_note: Engineering decision applied in the Round 11 campaign ('owner may override'); overridden by the Oct 31 owner safety clarifications where they differ. Text: New drafts start with no moves in every generation, and choosing a species never auto-fills moves. Existing Pokémon keep their moves; H28's passing behaviour (incompatible moves are cleared on a species change) stays. Keep/Add requires at least one move because a moveless Pokémon is not usable in game.

title: Decision: Required fields
doc_note: Engineering decision applied in the Round 11 campaign ('owner may override'); overridden by the Oct 31 owner safety clarifications where they differ. Text: Create requires the fields the native format and writer need: Met Location in Gen III–V (Gen V already does), at least one move everywhere. Gen I has no met data and Gold/Silver have none; Crystal caught data stays optional (legitimately blank for traded Pokémon). The suggested "level 100 should have 1–2 moves" rule is **not** a game rule and is not invented.

title: Decision: Actions menu
doc_note: Engineering decision applied in the Round 11 campaign ('owner may override'); overridden by the Oct 31 owner safety clarifications where they differ. Text: Every generation offers the same order — View, Edit, Clone, Move, Release, Origin & Legality, Export to file, Review pending changes, Cancel — showing only actions that really work. Move to Vault is not shown until the Vault exists.

title: Decision: Recovery files
doc_note: Engineering decision applied in the Round 11 campaign ('owner may override'); overridden by the Oct 31 owner safety clarifications where they differ. Text: The global list stays (protection is computed over the full listing); focus starts on the opening game's group, preferably its first removable copy.

title: Decision: Box controls
doc_note: Engineering decision applied in the Round 11 campaign ('owner may override'); overridden by the Oct 31 owner safety clarifications where they differ. Text: Y picks up, A places, B cancels (all generations). X exports on an occupied slot and imports on an empty slot; Create stays in Actions.

title: Create validation is exact-game / format-aware
owner_words: **Create validation is exact-game / format-aware.** "At least one move" is an **app policy** for a usable Pokémon, not a legality proof, and is labelled as such. Met Location is required as an **explicit choice** in the exact game's own location list. Never require a *nonzero* value: a real native Pokémon can legitimately carry location 0 or no recorded location (for example Gen III RSE index 0, Gen IV/V special or "----" entries, traded or event records). The check must use each game's native semantics, never one universal rule.
doc_note: Owner safety clarification (October 31); overrides section 4 decisions where they differ. Owner words as recorded in the intake (bold markup retained).

title: H25 history vs stale editor state
owner_words: **H25 history vs stale editor state.** On an existing Pokémon, recorded history (Met Location, Met Level, Pokérus, ball, egg/fateful data) is **preserved**. When it is incompatible with a newly chosen species, it is **flagged** in the editor and in Review, never silently deleted. New drafts reset properly and never inherit another record's state; the editor panels always re-read the record being edited, so nothing stale is shown.
doc_note: Owner safety clarification (October 31); overrides section 4 decisions where they differ. Owner words as recorded in the intake (bold markup retained).

title: Recovery files
owner_words: **Recovery files.** Focus may start on the current game's backups, but **nothing starts selected for deletion**. All protection (newest copy, Bank, unverified) and both confirmation steps stay exactly as they are.
doc_note: Owner safety clarification (October 31); overrides section 4 decisions where they differ. Owner words as recorded in the intake (bold markup retained).

title: [MANDATORY 2] Master Vault v1 core invariants
doc_note: "Original imported Pokémon bytes are immutable. Every stored entity has a stable internal Vault ID. Every raw payload is hashed with SHA-256. Origin and current location are separate concepts. Derived Pokémon never overwrite their parent. ... All persistent mutations are transactional and recoverable. Live game-save writing is outside the Vault transaction and remains disabled until the separate save-write safety contract is met."

title: Vault on-disk separation (entities/metadata/provenance/indexes/transactions, banks, backups)
doc_note: "The exact serialization can evolve, but v1 should preserve this separation"; SQLite migration "allowed only if the same invariants remain true and a safe migration path exists".

title: Vault insert/modify transaction with journal; no partially published entity visible
doc_note: BEGIN -> journal -> temp write -> fsync -> SHA-256 -> parse/validate -> atomic publish -> update indexes -> verify -> COMMIT; on failure ABORT and restore. "No partially published Vault entity should appear in normal browsing."

title: Vault startup crash recovery; never guess partial payload valid
doc_note: "inspect pending transaction journals ... verify hashes ... finish only provably safe metadata/index publication steps ... otherwise roll back references and quarantine incomplete data. Never guess that a partially written payload is valid."

title: Versioned schema migration with metadata backup; unknown newer schema opens read-only
doc_note: "make a Vault metadata backup before migration; raw Pokémon payload files are not rewritten merely to migrate metadata; ... unknown newer schema versions open read-only rather than being overwritten"

title: Import must not silently discard duplicates
doc_note: "Default import behavior should not silently discard data merely because a hash already exists."

title: Banks are references; deleting a Bank never deletes Vault entities
doc_note: "A Vault entity may appear in multiple banks without duplicating raw storage. Deleting a bank does not delete Vault entities. Permanent Vault deletion, if implemented at all, must be a separate explicit operation with recovery/backup semantics."

title: Vault must scale without loading all raw Pokémon into RAM
doc_note: "lazy entity loading; compact indexes; bounded caches; metadata-first browsing; ... no full-Vault raw scan on every app launch unless recovery/integrity verification requires it"
